section.sectionSummaryBrief: The distinction between a miracle occurring by day or by night corresponds to whether the miracle is in a manner of revelation or concealment.
section.t: And it may be said,
that the distinction in the time when the miracle occurred,
day or night,
corresponds to the level and manner of the miracle,
whether the miracle is in a manner of light and revelation
(day)
or whether it is in a manner of concealment
(night).
And based on this, it may also be sweetened that the miracle is in a manner of day,
light and revelation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: A miracle, from the term meaning "elevation," elevates nature and the time and place in which it occurs.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter
(the connection of the time when the miracle occurred to the miracle)
will be understood by prefacing the known concept that a miracle (nes) is from the term meaning elevation (herim).
For through the miracle, an elevation and ascent is made in nature.
And this is what we say, "Blessed is He who performed a miracle for me in this place,"
for even the place, which is boundary and nature, is elevated through the miracle that is above nature.
And from this it is understood that the same applies regarding the time in which the miracle occurred,
and as we say in the blessing of the miracles
(of Chanukah and Purim)
that He performed miracles for our forefathers in those days, at this time.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: There are two general types of miracles: those above nature and those clothed in nature, with two subcategories regarding the concealment of the miracle within its natural garment.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter in more detail,
it is known
that in miracles there are
(generally)
two types.
Miracles that are above nature
[like the miracles that were in the Exodus from Egypt,
the turning of water to blood, etc., and up to the miracle of the Splitting of the Sea, when the sea became dry land],
and miracles that are clothed in natural ways.
And within these themselves, there are two manners.
The natural garments are in a manner that it is recognizable in them that they are only a garment for the miracle that is clothed within them.
Like the miracles of Chanukah and Purim
(and similarly the miracles of the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev
and Yud Beis Tammuz),
for even though they are clothed in natural ways,
nevertheless, it was recognizably revealed
(to the extent that "all the ends of the earth saw")
the miracle within them.
And the natural garments conceal and hide the miracle that is clothed within them.
To the extent that sometimes they conceal and hide it completely,
so that it is not recognizable at all that it is a miracle,
"the master of the miracle does not recognize his miracle."
